turns.question: I have a multivariate monthly time series with five unnamed series (series_1 through series_5). Can you profile the dataset — tell me about its length, frequency, any missing data, and provide a statistical overview?
turns.response:
# Dataset Profile

## Basic Structure

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Rows (observations)** | 54 |
| **Columns** | 6 (1 date + 5 series) |
| **Start date** | 1990-01-01 |
| **End date** | 1994-06-01 |
| **Frequency** | Monthly (calendar months, first-of-month timestamps) |
| **Coverage** | 4 years, 6 months (Jan 1990 – Jun 1994) |
| **Missing values** | **None** — every cell in every row is populated |

All five series are numeric (float-compatible) and the date column is a clean ISO-formatted monthly timestamp with no gaps or duplicate periods.

## Statistical Overview

| Series | Min | Max | Mean | Sample Std | CV (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| series_1 | 480 | 9,000 | 3,522.2 | 1,954.4 | 55.5% |
| series_2 | 120 | 7,440 | 1,573.3 | 1,372.3 | 87.2% |
| series_3 | 720 | 8,760 | 3,926.7 | 1,810.7 | 46.1% |
| series_4 | 180 | 7,780 | 2,690.4 | 1,997.3 | 74.2% |
| series_5 | 600 | 12,050 | 5,830.6 | 3,228.7 | 55.4% |

Supporting totals (sum over 54 months):

| Series | Sum |
|---|---:|
| series_1 | 190,200 |
| series_2 | 84,960 |
| series_3 | 212,040 |
| series_4 | 145,280 |
| series_5 | 314,850 |

## Key Observations

- **Scale differences are large.** Series_5 has the highest mean (~5,831) and the widest absolute range (600–12,050), while series_2 is the smallest on average (~1,573) and also the most volatile in relative terms (CV ≈ 87%). Any cross-series modeling should consider standardization/normalization.

- **series_2 is the most volatile relatively** (CV 87.2%), with frequent drops to the floor value of 120 (appearing in 1990-03, 1991-05, 1993-04, 1993-09). This suggests a possible lower bound or recurring near-zero regime.

- **series_3 is the most stable relatively** (CV 46.1%), staying mostly in the 2,000–6,000 band with a single spike to 8,760 in 1993-09.

- **series_5 shows the heaviest tails**, with several extreme highs (12,050 in 1990-12; 11,500 in 1991-08; 12,000 in 1993-12; 11,550 in 1994-01) — worth flagging as potential outliers or seasonal/year-end effects.

- **No missing data and a regular monthly cadence** mean the series are directly comparable on a common time index without imputation or resampling.

If you'd like, I can next look at seasonality, trend, cross-correlations, or outlier diagnostics on any of these series.

turns.question: Do any of these series exhibit seasonal patterns? Check for annual (12-month) seasonality across all five.
How are the five series correlated with one another at lag 0? Identify any pairs that move together.
turns.response:
# Lag-0 Correlation Analysis

## Correlation Matrix (Pearson, contemporaneous)

| | series_1 | series_2 | series_3 | series_4 | series_5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **series_1** | 1.00 | **0.27** | 0.10 | 0.01 | −0.03 |
| **series_2** | **0.27** | 1.00 | 0.08 | 0.08 | 0.00 |
| **series_3** | 0.10 | 0.08 | 1.00 | **0.65** | **0.50** |
| **series_4** | 0.01 | 0.08 | **0.65** | 1.00 | **0.42** |
| **series_5** | −0.03 | 0.00 | **0.50** | **0.42** | 1.00 |

## Key Findings

### A correlated cluster: series_3 ↔ series_4 ↔ series_5

The three strongest pairwise correlations all involve series 3, 4, and 5:

| Pair | Correlation | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| **series_3 & series_4** | **0.65** | Moderate-to-strong positive; the tightest pair in the dataset |
| **series_3 & series_5** | **0.50** | Moderate positive |
| **series_4 & series_5** | **0.42** | Moderate-weak positive |

These three series tend to rise and fall together month-to-month. Supporting examples:

- **Sep 1993:** s3 = 8,760, s4 = 6,720, s5 = 11,150 — all near their respective highs
- **Dec 1993:** s4 = 7,780, s5 = 12,000 — both peak together
- **Jan 1994:** s3 = 7,680, s4 = 4,360, s5 = 11,550 — all elevated
- **May 1994:** s3 = 1,710, s4 = 2,740, s5 = 2,700 — all relatively low

### A weak link: series_1 & series_2

| Pair | Correlation | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| **series_1 & series_2** | **0.27** | Weak positive; the only other pair above 0.20 |

This is driven largely by a few co-occurring spikes (e.g., Jan 1991: s1 = 5,640, s2 = 6,120; Jul 1992: s1 = 5,880, s2 = 7,440), but the relationship is inconsistent across the full series.

### Essentially uncorrelated pairs

All remaining pairs have |r| < 0.15:

| Pair | Correlation |
|---|---:|
| s1–s3 | 0.10 |
| s2–s3 | 0.08 |
| s2–s4 | 0.08 |
| s1–s4 | 0.01 |
| s2–s5 | 0.00 |
| s1–s5 | −0.03 |

## Summary

The dataset has **one clear correlated block** — series_3, series_4, and series_5 move together — with series_3 acting as the hub (it correlates most strongly with both of the others). Series_1 and series_2 are largely independent of this block and of each other, aside from a faint link between them. If you're building a multivariate model, the s3–s4–s5 cluster is where multicollinearity would be a concern.
